Instructions for the project.

You are building a browser-based prototype named “ACBJ Survey Navigator.”

The product is a guided, adaptive business survey inspired by the interaction model of consumer tax-preparation software. It should feel bright, clean, spacious, reassuring and conversational rather than like a long information form.

Core product rules:
1. Show primarily one question or one closely related group per screen.
2. Use configuration-driven questions and modules rather than hard-coded page flows.
3. Support previous/next navigation, autosave, resume and section-based progress.
4. Use existing company information when available and ask respondents to confirm or update it.
5. Display only questions relevant to the respondent’s answers.
6. Keep required research questions separate from optional editorial questions.
7. Keep ownership structure separate from voluntary ownership description.
8. Never infer ownership descriptions from names, photos, biographies or other indirect information.
9. Include a persistent BizEstimate area, but use only clearly labeled synthetic demonstration values in v1.
10. Do not invent a production valuation formula, complete industry taxonomy or production NAICS mapping.
11. Build accessible, responsive interfaces suitable for desktop and mobile.
12. Preserve all accepted functionality from earlier stages.

At the end of each stage:
- Run the project build, linting and test suite.
- Fix failures before stopping.
- Summarize files changed, tests run, known limitations and the stage acceptance checklist.
- Do not begin the next stage unless asked.
